english_retrieval.title: Supreme (brand)
english_retrieval.snippet: # Supreme (brand). **Supreme** is an American clothing brand established in Manhattan, New York City, in April 1994. The brand was founded in 1994 by American-British businessman and fashion designer James Jebbia. During the formation of the brand, Jebbia was inspired by a book on Barbara Kruger's artwork, which influenced the design of Supreme's red box logo with a white Futura "Futura (typeface)") Heavy Oblique font. The first store was opened in a former office space on Lafayette Street in Lower Manhattan in April 1994. The store's first employees included skaters and actors, such as Justin Pierce and Harold Hunter, as well as other cast members from the Larry Clark film *Kids "Kids (film)").* Jebbia said that he opened Supreme in Lower Manhattan because there were few options for buying skateboarding products in that area at the time. Supreme's first artist collaboration was with Rammellzee in 1994, the year the brand opened its first store in New York City; the partnership produced hand-painted trucker hats and backpacks.

merged_results.title: Supreme (brand)
merged_results.snippet: # Supreme (brand). **Supreme** is an American clothing brand established in Manhattan, New York City, in April 1994. The brand was founded in 1994 by American-British businessman and fashion designer James Jebbia. During the formation of the brand, Jebbia was inspired by a book on Barbara Kruger's artwork, which influenced the design of Supreme's red box logo with a white Futura "Futura (typeface)") Heavy Oblique font. The first store was opened in a former office space on Lafayette Street in Lower Manhattan in April 1994. The store's first employees included skaters and actors, such as Justin Pierce and Harold Hunter, as well as other cast members from the Larry Clark film *Kids "Kids (film)").* Jebbia said that he opened Supreme in Lower Manhattan because there were few options for buying skateboarding products in that area at the time. Supreme's first artist collaboration was with Rammellzee in 1994, the year the brand opened its first store in New York City; the partnership produced hand-painted trucker hats and backpacks.
